exposure: Women who desired to keep their fertility
outcome: International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire on vaginal symptoms (ICIQ-VS) score
cohort: 42 women who underwent laparoscopic sacrohysteropexy for Pelvic Organ Prolapse—Quantification (POP-Q) stage ≥2 uterovaginal prolapse from January 2007 to May 2017.
finding: Laparoscopic sacrohysteropexy is an effective and feasible procedure for the management of uterovaginal prolapse in young women who wish to preserve their uteri.
mod_finding: Of the 13 pregnancies in the study, 10 women underwent caesarean sections with no recurrences of prolapse noted on postpartum follow-ups, and one woman delivered vaginally 11 months after surgery and presented with a recurrent prolapse.
